intro.label: LESS BETWEEN YOU AND THE PART
intro.title:
Make the small thing
that makes a difference.
intro.description: A bracket that fits. An enclosure that closes. A replacement that keeps something working. Build functional parts with dimensions you can come back and change.
intro.bracketBody: Position holes, set clearances, and adapt a part to the space it needs to fit.
intro.enclosureBody: Build solids, hollow them with Shell, and add holes and edge treatments.
intro.replacementBody: Capture dimensions as variables and refine the design through editable history.

features.label: PRECISION, WITH ROOM TO CHANGE
features.title:
Real geometry.
Useful control.
features.description: Sketch-based parametric CAD, exact B-Rep solids, and a model history that keeps your intent editable.
features.sketchBody: Draw profiles with lines, arcs, circles, and curves. Add dimensions and constraints, then reuse document variables and expressions.
features.solidBody: Extrude and revolve profiles. Add lofts, sweeps, booleans, holes, fillets, chamfers, and shells through persistent features.
features.assemblyBody: Organize parts, reuse local library components, and explore assemblies with mates, joints, and interference inspection.
features.printBody: Export 3MF, STEP, or STL. Keep an editable native backup, and use the paired local bridge for supported desktop slicers.
features.privacyBody: Model computation and browser storage stay on your device by default. Export a native backup to keep a portable copy of your work.
features.agentBody: Connect an external MCP client to a paired browser session. Discover supported tools, inspect drafts, and control how changes are applied.
features.scope: Capabilities vary between the editor and MCP. See the feature matrix and current release gates.

workflow.label: FROM A DIMENSION TO A REAL THING
workflow.title: A short path to your next part.
workflow.description: Keep the design editable all the way to export.
workflow.sketchTitle: Start with what has to fit.
workflow.sketchBody: Choose a plane, draw a closed profile, and add the dimensions that matter. Use variables for sizes you expect to change.
workflow.shapeBody: Extrude the profile into an exact solid. Add holes, edge treatments, and other features, then revisit their parameters through history.
workflow.exportBody: Save a native backup for later edits. Export 3MF for a print workflow, STEP for CAD exchange, or STL for a triangle mesh.
workflow.illustrative: Workflow illustration · not a live CAD session

ai.title:
Describe the intent.

ai.inspect: Inspect the current model and available tools
ai.review: Review and apply, or use authorized session auto-apply

Your browser is
a good workshop.
downloads.description: Open the hosted editor, run from source, or prepare a portable local package. No cloud CAD account is required.
downloads.browserBody: Start in the hosted editor. Models are stored in this browser by default; export a native backup for portability.
downloads.localBody: Run the editor locally with the pinned Bun version, or build a portable package from verified, committed source.
downloads.installerBody: Signed VibeShape installers for macOS, Windows, and Linux are not currently available. The existing OCCT source archive is not an application installer.

faq.title: A few useful answers.
faq.priceA: Yes. VibeShape is free, open source software licensed under GPL-3.0-or-later. External agent providers and other services have their own terms.
faq.offlineA: Yes. Run the source checkout with the pinned Bun version or prepare a portable local package. The portable runtime needs Bun installed. Offline web operation and updates have separate release gates; do not assume a first visit works without a network connection.
faq.aiQ: Do I need an AI subscription?
faq.aiA: Manual CAD modeling does not require an AI model. Agent-assisted workflows use a separately configured MCP client; that client supplies its own model access.
faq.filesQ: What files can I take out?
faq.filesA: Use the native .vshape format for editable backups. Export committed geometry as 3MF, STEP, or STL, depending on your next tool. The slicer, printer settings, and physical print validation remain separate steps.

getting-started.title: Your first part
getting-started.summary: From a blank project to an editable solid and an export.
getting-started.intro: Begin with a small part whose key dimensions you know. A simple plate or bracket is a useful first project.
getting-started.one: Open the editor and create a project. Choose a sketch plane and draw a closed profile. Give important lengths dimensions; use document variables for values you will want to reuse.
getting-started.two: Extrude the closed profile. Add supported features such as holes, fillets, or chamfers. Preview changes before applying them and revisit earlier parameters through history.
getting-started.three: Browser autosave belongs to the current browser and origin. Export an editable .vshape backup, then choose 3MF, STEP, or STL for the downstream workflow. Check the exported part in your next tool.

local-installation.title: Run VibeShape locally
local-installation.summary: Use the source checkout or prepare a portable local package.
local-installation.intro: The source workflow uses the Bun version pinned in the repository packageManager field. At the time this site was prepared, that version is Bun 1.4.2. Native signed desktop installers are not published yet.
local-installation.one: Install the pinned Bun version, clone the repository, install dependencies, and start Vite. Open the Local URL printed by the development server. This is a development checkout; controlled production and kernel builds have additional preparation steps.
local-installation.two: The packager consumes a verified editor build and committed source. Follow the portable distribution reference for controlled build preparation, licensing assets, packaging, installation, updates, and rollback. Do not treat a source archive as a ready-to-run application.
local-installation.three: The portable package needs Bun on PATH; it does not bundle Bun. Its runtime does not need a source checkout, node_modules, a cloud account, or a model API. The documented launcher and installer workflow targets macOS and Linux; Windows desktop installers are not yet available.

parametric-modeling.title: Model with design intent
parametric-modeling.summary: Profiles, constraints, variables, features, and editable history.
parametric-modeling.intro: Parametric modeling records how a part is made. Change an input dimension and the dependent features can rebuild from that intent.
parametric-modeling.one: Use sketch geometry and dimensional constraints to define a closed profile. Keep meaningful sizes in variables and expressions rather than repeatedly entering the same value.
parametric-modeling.two: Use Extrude, Revolve, and other supported features to construct the solid. Keep parts organized and use measurements to inspect dimensions. The feature matrix describes the implemented scope and open work.
parametric-modeling.three: An invalid or ambiguous reference is a repair task. Inspect the failed feature and its intended geometry instead of assuming that a visually plausible result preserves the design.

mcp.title: Connect your agent with MCP
mcp.summary: Pair a browser session, inspect a model, and apply supported changes.
mcp.intro: VibeShape works with an external MCP client. The browser has no embedded chat: your client supplies the agent and model. Tool discovery is the authority for what that session can do. Remote MCP is not yet enabled at cad.hello-world.cz. For agent workflows, use the local MCP setup below.
mcp.one: For a source checkout, complete the controlled build prerequisites linked from the MCP quickstart, then run bun ci and bun run prepare:local to build the editor before starting the stdio MCP server. Configure your client according to the quickstart, using Bun with the absolute path to apps/mcp-server/src/index.ts. The bun run mcp:local shortcut requires the checkout working directory.
mcp.two: Use the URL and pairing flow described in the quickstart. Open or import the project, then explicitly enable the AI session. The pairing origin has separate browser storage from the ordinary development origin.
mcp.three: Discover the current tools and inspect the model before authoring. Drafts are disposable. Changes normally use reviewed application; optional session auto-apply changes that policy when explicitly enabled. Disable the AI session to revoke access.

export-and-print.title: Export and prepare to print
export-and-print.summary: Choose between native backups, CAD exchange, and print meshes.
export-and-print.intro: Keep the editable design and the downstream manufacturing file as separate deliverables. An export is a handoff, not proof that the part will print successfully.
export-and-print.one: Export .vshape to preserve the editable project. Browser autosave is tied to an origin and a browser profile, so it is not a replacement for a file backup.
export-and-print.two: Use STEP for exact CAD exchange, or 3MF and STL for mesh-based downstream workflows. Inspect scale, orientation, clearances, and the result in the receiving tool.
export-and-print.three: The explicitly paired local Slicer Bridge can launch an allowlisted desktop slicer with the generated 3MF. If pairing or launch is unavailable, the editor falls back to downloading the file. Slicing, G-code, printer operation, and physical validation remain separate.

privacy.title: Your files and your device
privacy.summary: Understand local storage, backups, and explicit connections.
privacy.intro: By default, computation, files, and model history stay on your device. A cloud account and mandatory telemetry are not required for the CAD workflow.
privacy.one: Projects stored at one origin or in one browser profile are separate from another. Clearing site data can remove local work. Export native backups before moving devices, changing browsers, or clearing storage.
privacy.two: MCP sessions and slicer handoff use pairing. External clients and model providers have their own policies; local CAD computation does not make an external agent provider local.
privacy.three: The security and privacy reference documents import boundaries, storage behavior, paired services, and remaining release gates. Use the current reference when choosing a deployment workflow.
